extracted.intended_audience: Researchers (postdoctoral applicants) and host institutions/supervisors preparing MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowship proposals; also useful for external evaluators
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation criteria and scoring rules used to assess Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Postdoctoral Fellowship proposals, describing the three weighted award criteria, scoring scale, thresholds, and the evaluation process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence (50% of the mark)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality and pertinence of the project's research and innovation objectives; soundness of the proposed methodology; quality of supervision, training, and two-way knowledge transfer (three-way for Global Fellowships) between the researcher and the host; quality and appropriateness of the researcher's professional experience, competencies, and skills; match between the researcher's profile, training-through-research, and the project objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the highest-weighted criterion (50%). Evaluators consider both the project aims and the researcher's capacity to carry them out: relevance of objectives, methodological robustness, supervision and training arrangements (including bi-directional transfer of knowledge with the host, or three-way transfer for Global Fellowships), the researcher's CV/track record and skills, and the fit between the researcher's background and the proposed training-through-research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact (30% of the mark)
rubrics_metrics.description: Credibility of measures to enhance the career perspectives and employability of the researcher; suitability and quality of measures to maximize expected outcomes and impacts (dissemination, exploitation, communication of project results); quality of activities to communicate the project to different audiences; public engagement strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators assess how the fellowship will improve the fellow's career and employability, and the plans to ensure outputs reach relevant audiences and stakeholders. Consider dissemination/exploitation/communication plans, outreach/public engagement activities, and concrete measures intended to maximize the project's expected outcomes and impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality and Efficiency of the Implementation (20% of the mark)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality and effectiveness of the work plan, assessment of risks and appropriateness of the effort; quality and capacity of the host institutions and participating organizations, including hosting arrangements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment focuses on the realism and coherence of the work plan and timeline, identification and mitigation of risks, allocation of resources and effort, and the host institution(s)' ability to support the project (infrastructure, supervision, hosting arrangements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring System
rubrics_metrics.description: Each criterion is scored from 0 to 5 with half-point resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thresholds: each individual criterion must reach a minimum of 3.0. Overall total threshold is 70% (i.e., 10.5 points overall when considering the three criteria out of a maximum 15). Use the weighted composition (Excellence 50%, Impact 30%, Implementation 20%) to compute the final score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation Process
rubrics_metrics.description: MSCA proposals are evaluated by at least 3 independent external expert evaluators against the award criteria defined in the work programme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals receive independent assessments from multiple external experts; panels apply the work programme's award criteria and thresholds. Note: typical success rates are low (around 10%), so achieving or exceeding thresholds and demonstrating strong excellence/impact/implementation is critical.
